text: 4.1 Experimental Setup Datasets and Evaluation Metrics. Our training corpus consists of three distinct datasets selected to balance faithful grounding with creative expression. For hallucination mitigation, we utilize the summarization subset of RAGTruth ( Niu et al., 2024 ) and the question-answering subset of HaluEval ( Li et al., 2023 ) . To support creative generation, we curate a subset of the Arena-Human-Preference-140k dataset from Chatbot Arena ( Chiang et al., 2024 ) , 1 1 1 https://huggingface.co/datasets/lmarena-ai/arena-human-preference-140k filtering specifically for prompts related to creative writing. All experiments are run once. For summarization, we evaluate on 831 source documents from the Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard dataset ( Hughes et al., 2023 ) , denoted HHEM in our tables. For QA, we use MultiHopRAG ( Tang and Yang, 2024 ) . Both hallucination rates are the percentage of generated responses judged hallucinated by our best-performing HA-GRM. General and creative writing capabilities are evaluated on the Hard Prompts and Creative Writing subsets of Arena-Hard-v2.0 , respectively, using its official pipeline ( Li et al., 2025 ) . 2 2 2 https://github.com/lmarena/arena-hard-auto Table 4 summarizes the statistics for all datasets. Baselines and Training Details. To evaluate HARPO, we compare it against three baselines: (1) Hallucination-Only , trained exclusively on RAGTruth and HaluEval using only R hallu R_{\text{hallu}} ; (2) Writing-Only , trained solely on Arena-Human-Preference-140k using only R creat R_{\text{creat}} ; and (3) Linear Mixture , a combined-objective baseline. Following Peng et al. (2025) , the Linear Mixture baseline performs multi-objective alignment via fixed scalarization. We normalize the writing reward to [ 0 , 1 ] [0,1] and compute the arithmetic mean with the hallucination reward: ( R creat norm + R hallu ) / 2 (R^{\text{norm}}_{\text{creat}}+R_{\text{hallu}})/2 . This serves as the primary state-of-the-art comparison for mixed-objective training. This baseline uses the same training data as HARPO but a different reward strategy. For reinforcement learning hyperparameters, we adopt the same configuration used to train HA-GRM. HARPO lowers HA-GRM-judged hallucination rates and improves writing scores relative to the corresponding base models. 4.2 Results and Analysis Main Results. Table 5 presents the performance of HARPO across different model families (Qwen2.5, Qwen3) and parameter scales (1.7B to 8B). Our analysis yields two key observations: 1. Trade-offs in Single-Objective Training: On Qwen3-4B, Hallucination-Only reaches the lowest HHEM hallucination rate (0.72%), while Creative Writing decreases from 16.95% to 9.74% and General decreases from 11.16% to 5.29% relative to the base model. Writing-Only raises Creative Writing from 16.95% to 43.35%, while the HHEM hallucination rate rises from 7.34% to 24.31%. These results show that optimizing either objective alone can improve its target metric while degrading another. 2. Improvements over Base Models: HARPO has lower HA-GRM-judged hallucination rates on both datasets and higher Creative Writing and General scores than the corresponding base models at every tested size. For example, on Qwen2.5-7B, the HHEM hallucination rate decreases from 5.05% to 1.56% and Creative Writing increases from 4.68% to 6.78%. These comparisons concern the base models; comparisons with other training strategies reveal additional trade-offs. Comparison with Linear Reward Mixing. For Qwen3-4B, HARPO has a lower HHEM hallucination rate than Linear Mixture (1.08% vs. 3.73%) and a higher General score (12.35% vs. 5.63%). However, its MultiHopRAG hallucination rate is slightly higher (1.02% vs. 0.90%), and its Creative Writing score is slightly lower (27.54% vs. 28.83%). HARPO therefore improves summarization faithfulness as judged by HA-GRM and performance on Hard Prompts, with a trade-off in QA hallucination rate and creative-writing score. SAM activates writing rewards only for responses judged hallucination-free by HA-GRM; this comparison reflects the complete HARPO training configuration. Effect of Data Curriculum Strategy. To validate our data curriculum strategy, we compare it against two alternative schedules as shown on the left of Figure 1 : (1) Random Mixture , which samples tasks with a fixed probability throughout training; and (2) Faithful → \to Creative , a reverse schedule that begins with hallucination mitigation and transitions to creative writing. Table 6 compares the reported curriculum outcomes. Relative to Random Mixture , Creative → \to Faithful lowers the HHEM hallucination rate from 4.09% to 1.08% and the MultiHopRAG rate from 1.17% to 1.02%, while increasing Creative Writing from 23.65% to 27.54%. The reverse Faithful → \to Creative schedule obtains the highest Creative Writing score (34.30%), but has higher hallucination rates on HHEM (9.64%) and MultiHopRAG (1.72%) than Creative → \to Faithful (1.08% and 1.02%). Thus, the proposed schedule favors lower HA-GRM-judged hallucination rates, with a lower creative-writing score than the reverse schedule. The preferred schedule depends on the relative priority of these metrics. Figure 2: Response length analysis on HHEM. Analysis of Response Length and Verbosity To investigate whether our framework mitigates “reward hacking”, specifically the tendency of RL-tuned models to inflate scores through verbosity, we track the evolution of response length throughout the training process (Figure 2 ). The Writing-Only baseline exhibits a linear, unbounded increase in token count, confirming that optimizing solely for creativity encourages excessive length. Conversely, the Hallucination-Only baseline rapidly converges to shorter, risk-averse responses, potentially sacrificing necessary detail to minimize hallucination rate. HARPO, however, demonstrates a distinct trajectory that balances these extremes. Initially, the response length increases, aligning with the high ratio of creative tasks in the early curriculum. However, as the training progresses beyond step 60, the length peaks and gradually stabilizes.
